analysis.title: GS Blekos - CPI Pre / GOAL / Europe Indus / LVMH / CTS Eventim / Orsted / Zurich Insurance 13 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS expects September core CPI at +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%), or +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%). Headline CPI is forecast at +0.59% (consensus +0.6%), reflecting higher energy prices.
GS's headline and core CPI forecasts are consistent with a slightly smaller +0.20% increase in September core PCE.

GOAL asset allocation update: overweight equities over 3 months, underweight credit over 3 months, overweight bonds over 12 months, and overweight cash tactically. Earnings growth remains supportive, and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the Q3 earnings season.

GS sees long-duration bonds offering better medium-term value as inflation normalises and central bank pricing becomes less hawkish. Tactically it still prefers shorter-duration fixed income (overweight cash).

Inventory cross-check: China's manufacturing inventories are above normal in September but have fallen recently. European inventories are steady but elevated. US inventories are lean on average, with only Machinery and Automotive significantly above long-run averages.
US electrical equipment inventories are at all-time lows. Depletion is seen across Metals, Machinery, Hardware, Manufacturing, Computer Equipment and Chemicals.

LVMH 3Q26 sales grew 1% at constant FX, in line with estimates (+1% GSe and Visible Alpha consensus). Fashion and Leather sales fell 5% cFX versus Visible Alpha consensus of -2% and GSe of -2.5%, after +1% in 2Q26. The Chinese cluster drove the slowdown, with sales down mid-teens in the quarter. Rating is Buy.

GS initiates CTS Eventim at Neutral with a EUR 68 price target. Eventim is Europe's leading ticketing and live entertainment platform and the global number two. Shares have de-rated about 50% over 18 months on rising competition and capital allocation concerns.

GS downgrades Orsted to Neutral with a new DKK 155 price target (about +15% upside). Reasons: European and US sovereign rates are up about 50-65 bp since late August (about 100 bp YTD) and Orsted is among the most capital-intensive companies in the sector. GS also expects Q3 results to be underwhelming versus the sector, risking negative consensus revisions. The upside is now below the sector average.
GS reinstates Zurich Insurance at Neutral. It targets an EPS CAGR above 9% for 2025-2027 excluding Beazley, with guided pro forma mid-single-digit EPS uplift from the Beazley deal.

Zurich's 1-year forward consensus P/E has compressed about 2.0x since April 2025. GS's 2027e P/E of 12.8x is at premiums of 0.5x to Allianz and 0.7x to Generali. Total capital return yield is at the low end of peers, but the spread over the local risk-free yield screens as attractive.

market_movers.rationale: LVMH (LVMH.PA) 3Q26 Fashion and Leather sales fell 5% cFX, worse than consensus of -2%, on a mid-teens drop in the Chinese cluster. GS keeps Buy.
CTS Eventim (EVDG.DE) is Europe's ticketing leader, but shares have de-rated about 50% over 18 months on competition and capital allocation concerns.
Orsted (ORSTED.CO) is capital-intensive in a rising-rate backdrop, Q3 is expected to be underwhelming, and the roughly +15% upside is below the sector average.
Zurich Insurance (ZURN.S) is reinstated at Neutral. Profit growth is attractive, but valuation and execution risk around Beazley balance it.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings growth is supportive and the valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into Q3 earnings. Overweight over 3 months.
GOAL moves to underweight credit over 3 months.
Overweight bonds over 12 months as inflation normalises and central bank pricing becomes less hawkish. Tactically prefers shorter duration and cash.
Inventories are at all-time lows, with depletion seen across several end markets.

earnings_insights: LVMH 3Q26 (reported): sales +1% cFX, in line with GSe and Visible Alpha consensus of +1%. Fashion and Leather -5% cFX versus Visible Alpha consensus -2% and GSe -2.5%, after +1% in 2Q26. Sales in the Chinese cluster were down mid-teens in the quarter.
Orsted: GS expects Q3 results to be somewhat underwhelming relative to the sector, which could lead to negative consensus earnings revisions (GS estimate, not yet reported).
Zurich: targeted EPS CAGR above 9% for 2025-2027 excluding Beazley (company target), with guided pro forma mid-single-digit EPS uplift from Beazley. GS 2027e P/E is 12.8x (GS estimate).
